title: Agents
text: pressfreedom R package bundling Shiny dashboard exploring Reporters Without Borders (RSF) Press Freedom Index. dashboard three views: Map — choropleth world, colored score/rank/dimension chosen year; low-friction entry point data. Trends — multi-country line charts (Score) bump charts (Rank) 2002–2025. Country — single country’s profile: horizontal Rank/Score stat table, score-band/rank-tier count bar charts, two combined trend charts (Score + dimensions, Rank + dimension ranks) sharing one deduplicated legend. Clicking country Map point Trends chart jumps Country profile (see “Shared navigation” ).

text: app uses fully modular design (inst/app/), built bslib::page_navbar() single id = "view" navset switching three nav_panel()s wired app.R: Map, Trends, Country. page_navbar()’s installed version (0.11.0) per-nav_panel() sidebar = argument — one page-level sidebar =, shared across panels — per-view sidebar content achieved navset_hidden(id = "sidebar_view") inside single sidebar, kept sync visible navbar tabs via nav_select("sidebar_view", input$view) observer server. mod_map — choropleth (plotly::plot_geo()) colored Score, Rank, 2022+ dimension. Year choices react zone metric (dimensions restrict 2022+, score 2013+). Score-like metrics use RSF’s real 5-class band classification; Rank uses percentile tiers — exposed independent checkboxGroupInput toggles grey (remove) unchecked bands. See “Map score/rank bands” . mod_chart (Trends) — renders plotly card, reused two contexts: standalone Trends view (multi-country, show_nav = TRUE) embedded Country view compact mode single country (show_nav = FALSE). Score → scatter line chart; Rank → ggbump bump chart converted via ggplotly(). interactive behavior (hover-dimming click--navigate) handled client-side via JavaScript (onRender) — see “Client-side JavaScript approach chart interactivity” . mod_country — flag/name header; overview card horizontal Rank/Score stat table (current/best/worst/mean--median/biggest advance/biggest decline) plus two small band/tier count bar charts (score bands via rsf_band(), rank tiers via rank_tier() per-year max_rank, reused mod_map.R); trend row two bespoke combined charts — Score (+ 5 context dimensions, 2022–2025) Rank (+ 5 dimension-rank columns, rank_pol etc.) — merged via plotly::subplot() one deduplicated, floating legend (dimension traces share legendgroup across panels; score panel’s copy sets showlegend = TRUE). hand-built plot_ly()/ggplot2+ggbump calls local mod_country.R, reuse mod_chart.R — see “Dimension data (2022+): per-view treatment” . mod_inputs (Trends sidebar) — selectInputs variable (Score/Rank — dimensions intentionally excluded, see ) country (multiple selection). helpers.R — df_chart() filters/prepares data; card_title() builds dynamic card header. flags.R — maps rwb_standardized$iso (alpha-3) flagon’s alpha-2 flag codes; see “Flags (flagon)” . app.R wires modules loads data via pressfreedom.data::rwb_standardized. module files use explicit package namespacing (e.g., shiny::, dplyr::) additional library() calls needed inside modules, except library(ggplot2) app.R (required ggplotly() resolves variables name search path). score_evolution scale-transition artifact (2013): RSF changed scoring methodology 2013, score_evolution (score - score_n_1) compares two incompatible scales one year, producing artifacts large +5,763 across dataset real year--year changes. rank_evolution unaffected (rank -year relative ordering years, regardless underlying score scale). Resolution: mod_country.R’s score stat block excludes year_n == 2013 “biggest gain”/“biggest drop” calculation (score_evolution set NA year, scoped locally — underlying rwb_standardized$score_evolution column untouched). use score_evolution elsewhere, apply exclusion surface artifact.

what: Nonce collision pitfall: identical values silently skip reactiveVal observers
title: Agents
text: Map Trends modules return list(country = ..., nonce = ...) app-level selected_country reactiveVal. nonce critical — reactiveVal silently skips calling observers assigned identical() value current one. fix (module-local integer counters): module used click_nonce <- 0 incremented 1 click. Clicking country map (nonce = 1) chart (nonce = 1) produced identical() values: silently broke navigation first chart click session (second clicks increment chart nonce beyond 1). Fix: Use .numeric(proc.time()[["elapsed"]]) instead integer counters. elapsed seconds since R process startup globally unique across modules re-executions: Apply pattern new module feeds selected_country reactiveVal needs distinguish repeated values.
code: # map click selected_country(list(country = "Algeria", nonce = 1))  # chart click on same country selected_country(list(country = "Algeria", nonce = 1))  # identical(), observer skipped # map click selected_country(list(country = "Algeria", nonce = 12345.678))  # chart click on same country selected_country(list(country = "Algeria", nonce = 12345.789))  # not identical(), observer fires

what: Client-side JavaScript approach for chart interactivity
title: Agents
text: interactive behavior Trends chart (click--navigate hover-dimming) now handled entirely client-side via JavaScript (htmlwidgets::onRender), rather R-side plotly event handlers plotlyProxy restyle commands. : Early attempts used R-side plotlyProxy() restyle hover dim non-hovered traces. first hover (client-side plotly traces fully initialized), triggered coerceTraceIndices error plotly’s JavaScript. error ran Shiny message batch navigation nav_select() triggered simultaneous click, error aborted entire message batch, silently swallowing navigation command. Current implementation: mod_chart.R’s renderPlotly, onRender callback installs three event listeners: Click--navigate: Extracts country name directly clicked trace (el.data[curveNumber].name, set plot_ly(color=) ggplot aes(color=)), calls Shiny.setInputValue() priority = 'event' ensure every click fires. Hover-dimming: Extracts hovered curveNumber, loops traces, sets opacities 1 hovered trace 0.15 others via Plotly.restyle() — instant, server round-trip. Unhover: Restores traces full opacity. design eliminates timing issue makes hover-dimming snappier. revert plotlyProxy restyle observeEvent(event_data("plotly_hover", ...)) — coerceTraceIndices error return.
